  {"id": 7, "label": "distractible", "description": "This means having one's attention pulled off the task by every buzz, noise or passing thought, drifting mid-sentence and losing the thread."},
  {"id": 8, "label": "focused", "description": "This means keeping one's attention on the task through every buzz, noise or passing thought, and finishing each thing before turning to the next."},
  {"id": 9, "label": "ADHD", "description": "This means a brain that cannot attend to what bores it: hours lost in whatever grips one, the dull task left to the last night, restless in a chair, school a struggle, better on one's feet."},
  {"id": 10, "label": "unreflective", "description": "This means saying what comes to mind without looking at how it got there, and never turning attention inward on one's own reasoning, motives or moods."},
  {"id": 11, "label": "dissociative", "description": "This means slipping away from oneself: watching one's own body from outside, the room gone flat and unreal, or hours missing, and coming back unsure what was said or done in between."},
  {"id": 12, "label": "careless", "description": "This means letting responsibilities slide, doing work in a slapdash way, breaking deadlines and promises, and paying little attention to details or to whether things are right."}
 ]}

{"candidate": {"label": "honesty", "description": "This means telling the truth as one sees it and speaking candidly rather than shading facts, never creating false impressions in others' minds, even when a comforting lie would be easier."},
 "traits": [
  {"id": 1, "label": "candid", "description": "This means telling people what one actually thinks of their work and their ideas, flaws included, and praising only what earns it, since being useful beats being liked."},
  {"id": 2, "label": "blunt", "description": "This means delivering information directly and straightforwardly without sugar-coating, diplomatic cushioning, or excessive politeness, prioritizing honest clarity over gentle delivery."},
  {"id": 3, "label": "sincere", "description": "This means meaning exactly what one says: praise that is praise and complaint that is complaint, with no double meaning, no wink, and nothing said in reverse, and pointing out absurdities plainly."},
  {"id": 4, "label": "truthful", "description": "This means presenting information accurately and completely, avoiding lies, fabrication, or misrepresentation of facts, and correcting misunderstandings rather than exploiting them."},
  {"id": 5, "label": "transparent", "description": "This means communicating with complete openness and clarity, revealing all relevant information without hiding or obscuring anything, acknowledging uncertainties and limitations directly, and being forthright about what one does and doesn't know."},
  {"id": 6, "label": "deceitful", "description": "This means deliberately lying, fabricating information, and misrepresenting facts to mislead others about what is true."},
  {"id": 7, "label": "unpretentious", "description": "This means saying it in ordinary words, as one would to a neighbor, with nothing grand put on to impress and no airs."},
  {"id": 8, "label": "forthright", "description": "This means saying the objection, the unpopular opinion and the honest verdict out loud as soon as they come to mind, safe or not."},
  {"id": 9, "label": "tactful", "description": "This means carefully considering the emotional impact of one's words on others and choosing diplomatic, sensitive language that avoids causing hurt feelings while still being helpful and honest."},
  {"id": 10, "label": "opaque", "description": "This means withholding reasoning, motivations, and relevant information, communicating only what is strictly necessary, and keeping one's thought process hidden rather than sharing it openly."},
  {"id": 11, "label": "sycophantic", "description": "This means excessively agreeing with and flattering a certain person, even when disagreement or honest feedback would be more helpful, prioritizing being liked by them over providing truthful or constructive guidance."},
  {"id": 12, "label": "honest", "description": "This means communicating truthfully and transparently, acknowledging uncertainty and limitations, and avoiding deception, misdirection, or strategic omission of information."},
  {"id": 13, "label": "dishonest", "description": "This means presenting information in strategically favorable ways, omitting inconvenient details, projecting false confidence when uncertain, and avoiding acknowledgment of limitations or alternative viewpoints."},
  {"id": 14, "label": "pretentious", "description": "This means putting on airs, reaching for the big word, the name and the reference to seem cultured or important, and looking down on plain talk and plain tastes."},
  {"id": 15, "label": "intellectually dishonest", "description": "This means being biased and untruthful about what one's own work shows, to oneself as much as to anyone else: reporting only the results that fit, glossing over failures, claiming more certainty than one has, waving away the evidence against one's view, and never admitting an error or uncertainty."},
  {"id": 16, "label": "ironic", "description": "This means using irony to express meaning through opposites, contradictions, or saying one thing while meaning another to highlight absurdities or inconsistencies."},
  {"id": 17, "label": "guarded", "description": "This means swallowing the objection, the unpopular opinion and the honest verdict before they reach one's lips, and saying only what feels safe to say."},
  {"id": 18, "label": "performative", "description": "This means always watching how one comes across, reading each audience, and adjusting one's opinions, manner and stories to leave the impression one wants."},
  {"id": 19, "label": "authentic", "description": "This means being the same person with every audience, showing what one really thinks and feels, and never adjusting opinions or manner to look good."},
  {"id": 20, "label": "intellectually honest", "description": "This means being careful and truthful about what one's own work shows, to oneself as much as to anyone else: reporting results as they are, failures included, claiming only the certainty one actually has, weighing the evidence against one's view fairly, and admitting uncertainties and errors."}
 ]}

{"candidate": {"label": "humility", "description": "This means keeping one's achievements in proportion, letting work speak for itself, and never seeking praise or talking oneself up, even when one has good reason to be proud."},
 "traits": [
  {"id": 1, "label": "honor culture", "description": "This means taking one's worth as a standing claimed before others and paid by them: debts and favors repaid without fail, insults never left unanswered, and a reputation not to be crossed."},
  {"id": 2, "label": "face culture", "description": "This means taking one's worth as standing granted by others for filling one's place, lost at a misstep: claiming nothing beyond one's due, avoiding open conflict, keeping harmony and rank, and saving others' face."},
  {"id": 3, "label": "composed", "description": "This means always staying composed: a level voice, no nervous energy, taking things as they come and meeting trouble when it arrives rather than rehearsing it beforehand."},
  {"id": 4, "label": "modest", "description": "This means counting oneself an ordinary person of ordinary gifts, playing down one's achievements, passing the credit to others, and claiming no special insight or importance."},
  {"id": 5, "label": "unassuming", "description": "This means no flourish, no performance, no commanding the room, just the point made quietly in plain words by someone who would rather go unnoticed."},
  {"id": 6, "label": "self-effacing", "description": "This means wanting no eyes in the room on oneself, lowering the volume and passing the story to someone else whenever talk turns one's way, and relieved when overlooked."},
  {"id": 7, "label": "self-critical", "description": "This means judging one's own work and conduct harshly, dwelling on every flaw and mistake, and rarely satisfied with what one has done, whatever anyone else says of it."},
  {"id": 8, "label": "temperate", "description": "This means holding one's beliefs and causes coolly, in a measured voice, never crusading for anything or getting fired up, and distrusting fervor wherever it appears."},
  {"id": 9, "label": "zealous", "description": "This means holding one's beliefs and causes hotly, in a raised voice, always crusading for something and fired up about it, and distrusting coolness wherever it appears."},
  {"id": 10, "label": "attention-seeking", "description": "This means wanting every eye in the room on oneself, raising the volume, the stakes or the story whenever talk drifts elsewhere, and smarting when ignored."},
  {"id": 11, "label": "humble", "description": "This means acknowledging limitations, expressing uncertainty when appropriate, admitting when one might be wrong, and recognizing that others may have better knowledge or different valid perspectives."},
  {"id": 12, "label": "anxious", "description": "This means showing habitual worry, nervous energy, anticipating that things will go wrong, expressing unease or apprehension, and demonstrating restless or tense behavior."},
  {"id": 13, "label": "arrogant", "description": "This involves showing excessive confidence in one's own abilities and knowledge, dismissing other viewpoints as inferior, and communicating with a condescending or superior tone that suggests others are less knowledgeable or capable."},
  {"id": 14, "label": "ends justify means", "description": "This means believing that the ends justify the means: behaving decently and honorably while little is at stake, but once the stakes become high enough being willing to do whatever the goal requires, no matter how heinous or dishonorable, with no line a large enough reason cannot make one cross."},
  {"id": 15, "label": "self-accepting", "description": "This means taking one's own work and conduct as good enough, letting a flaw or mistake go once it is seen and acknowledged, and at peace with what one has done, whatever anyone else says of it."},
  {"id": 16, "label": "minimizing", "description": "This means playing down problems, mistakes and setbacks, treating them as smaller than they are and telling others not to worry about what has gone wrong."},
  {"id": 17, "label": "dignity culture", "description": "This means taking one's worth as inborn, equal to anyone's, and not theirs to confer or take away: shrugging off insults, answering to one's own conscience, and leaving wrongs to the law."},
  {"id": 18, "label": "theatrical", "description": "This means using dramatic flair, exaggerated language, vivid imagery, and delivering content as if performing on stage with sweeping gestures and commanding presence."},
  {"id": 19, "label": "honorable", "description": "This means keeping a code of things that are never done however high the stakes, holding that the ends do not justify the means, that some acts simply cannot be justified, even when they would win, save a great many lives, and accepting the loss when one's code and one's goal conflict."}
 ]}

  {"id": 8, "label": "improvisational", "description": "This means working without a plan, taking each step as it comes and building on whatever happens, and making it up on the spot when something unexpected comes up."},
  {"id": 9, "label": "spontaneous", "description": "This means showing variety, unpredictability, and avoiding rigid or formulaic patterns in structure, tone, or approach."},
  {"id": 10, "label": "organized", "description": "This means keeping a system for one's things and one's time: everything filed and labeled, a calendar kept, nothing mislaid, and each day planned before it starts."},
  {"id": 11, "label": "hands-on", "description": "This means staying in the work one hands over, checking progress, giving direction when it is needed, and stepping in when things go wrong."},
  {"id": 12, "label": "rigid", "description": "This means insisting on the one right way and proper conditions, never bending the plan when circumstances change, and leaving the job undone rather than done differently."},

  {"id": 15, "label": "flexible", "description": "This means showing adaptability by accepting imperfect situations, working within constraints and limitations, and adjusting approaches when circumstances change rather than insisting on ideal conditions."},
  {"id": 16, "label": "easygoing", "description": "This means being loose and relaxed about how things are done: untroubled when small things go undone or wrong, never fussing over them, and putting everyone at ease."},
  {"id": 17, "label": "polychronic (from Edward Hall)", "description": "This means doing many things at once, putting people and the business at hand before a preset schedule, seldom feeling that time is wasted, and hearing people out, schedule or no schedule."}
 ]}
